Sentence (English): - Motivation for Purchase: We already have various household appliances like a robot vacuum and a food waste disposer!
Comments (English): [ Best home appliances I bought this year ] || ---------------- || - Motivation for Purchase: We already have various household appliances like a robot vacuum and a food waste disposer! Since there aren't that many dishes even when two of us eat, I didn't think a dishwasher was really necessary and hadn't bought one. However, someone suggested we give it a try, so I did some research and ended up purchasing it. - Reasons to Recommend Purchase: 1) Ample Storage. Many people say that the 2-3 person capacity model is actually more suitable for single-person households! I highly recommend the 6-person capacity model, especially for those who mainly eat Korean food, have many side dishes, or are 2-person households that generate a lot of dishes from cooking themselves! 2) Value for Money. I started looking into non-drilling 2-3 person dishwashers. When I actually went to buy one, the price was similar to the 6-person model. So, after reading various reviews, I found this product to be affordable among the 6-person models and was on sale on Coupang, so I grabbed it right away. - Review: 1) Appearance. I purchased the all-white version and am extremely satisfied! There was a price difference of 10,000 to 20,000 won depending on the color! I was considering buying the pink one because it was the cheapest, but I just bought the one I liked and I am extremely satisfied! 2) Cleaning Power. My concerns about how well it would clean were completely unfounded; it cleans even better than you might have expected, and you will see dishes dried cleanly without any water stains. I really think I made the right choice buying it. 3) Drilling Requirement. A Samsung technician comes to install this product! However, there is a condition! This applies only if you drill a hole in the sink or connect it using the standard method. Since I am renting, I could not drill a hole, so I searched online and connected the water supply pipe using the faucet near the sink. As a result, I only received support up to the delivery stage. However, I am satisfied because I don't have to deal with the hassle of contacting the landlord regarding the drilling. There is a minor inconvenience, though, as it does not have automatic water supply, so you have to supply water while the dishwasher is running. 4) Detergent. Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Comments (English): [ This is something that will pay off even if you use it well for just one year. ] || ---------------- || This is an honest and subjective review based on 2 months of actual use, purchased with my own money. Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Comments (English): [ This is something that will pay off even if you use it well for just one year. ] || ---------------- || This is an honest and subjective review based on 2 months of actual use, purchased with my own money. Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Comments (English): [ This is something that will pay off even if you use it well for just one year. ] || ---------------- || This is an honest and subjective review based on 2 months of actual use, purchased with my own money. Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!
