It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Comments (English): [ This is something that will pay off even if you use it well for just one year. ] || ---------------- || This is an honest and subjective review based on 2 months of actual use, purchased with my own money. Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Product Name: Samsung Electronics BESPOKE Countertop Dishwasher (6-Place Capacity). Automatic Door Opening Capability: Automatic. Release Year: 2021. KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

KC Certification Information: ZU07193-21002, RR-SEC-DW30A3030CE. Reason for Purchase: I placed one at my parents' house and bought another identical one for my home. It has been about two months since I purchased it, so I would like to leave another review of my experience using it during that time. Have you experienced any inconveniences during use? I haven't really noticed any inconveniences while using it. However, since we are a two-person household, when there aren't many dishes after breakfast or a simple meal, I gather them in the sink and run the wash, but that feels a bit unsanitary. I heard that water pools in dishes with concave backs? The more concave the back, the more water pools. But rather than flipping rice bowls exactly 180 degrees... If you utilize the plate rack well and insert the dishes at a 45-degree angle, water pooling is slightly less. Detergent recommendation? I haven't tried other detergents yet, but I do not recommend the detergent for the Tamron 6-place dishwasher. It leaves a lot of water stains. This is definitely a detergent issue. Cleaning power? You have to be good at "Tetris" for this. Since water sprays out from the bottom like a fountain, you need to create space for the water to rise. Plates stacked directly on top of wide dishes or frying pans won't get cleaned at all. Cleaning space for frying pans, pots, etc.? First, stack the plates and dishes neatly in layers. Then, place an inverted frying pan or pot at the very end. Water seeps into the gaps between the dishes, allowing for good cleaning. (See photo). You just need to make sure there is enough space for the blades on the ceiling to rotate. Which mode do you use the most? I usually run Standard / Quick mode with High Temperature Sterilization + Powerful Drying applied together. If you stack the dishes well using Tetris, this is usually enough to clean them well. Is pre-washing essential? Things like rice grains stuck to bowls, melted and solidified mozzarella cheese, dried ssamjang stuck to dishes, etc. Even on the standard mode, some residue remains. Just rinsing roughly in the sink with a scrubbing brush and running the dishwasher is sufficient. How are food scraps disposed? There is a mesh-like device at the bottom under the dishwasher blades, similar to a sink food scrap collector. You just need to clean it occasionally when food accumulates there. Water consumption? The product specifications state a water consumption of 8.7L per cycle. I am not sure which mode this refers to, but it might not be a small amount. However, those who usually leave the water running continuously to wash large quantities of dishes will likely use that much. For households with small sinks like mine, filling up the water and letting it run continuously can be cumbersome. Since there are cases where this happens, I think standards will vary from household to household. A word of caution? For thin, wide silicone, use high-temperature sterilization and powerful drying. After using them, the shape warped a little. Conclusion: I believe that no matter which dishwasher you buy, it is impossible to satisfy everyone 100%. However, this is a product I recommend purchasing "nevertheless." Especially for homes where there is no space in the kitchen or built-in installation is not possible, for those who find dishwasher prices burdensome, and for 2-3 person households looking for a cost-effective dishwasher. I just want to tell you to buy it. It is less of a burden than dishwashers costing over a million won, and it is worth the price. I think you have gotten your money's worth if you use this dishwasher well for just one year. Have a great day! I hope my review was helpful!

Sentence (English): I was excited when I saw that Costco began stocking Bosch dishwashers.
Comments (English): [ Nowhere Near Meeting Expectations ] || ---------------- || I was excited when I saw that Costco began stocking Bosch dishwashers. When I bought this a little over 3 months ago, they did not have any of the higher series, e.g., 800. We had been hoping to get rid of our old whirlpool for quite a while. it worked well enough, but it was ludicrously loud. Shipping was much faster than the original estimate, and the pickup and installation went well enough. Then. The Dishwasher 1. This thing is not as quiet as I expected, though it's totally acceptable and orders of magnitude quieter than our old one. 2. This thing does NOT clean well. We have tried everything - filling the rinse reserve, powder detergent, pod detergent, Lemi-shine, only filling it up 1/2 to 2/3 so things are spread out, making sure we run the hot water before starting it. Virtually every time, anywhere from a few to nearly half of the dishes are not clean. We have taken to essentially prewashing dishes before loading them. This is NOT what we were looking for when we bought a new Bosch dishwasher. Costco 1. I love Costco. Truly. They have almost uniformly taken great care of us over the last 20+ years of membership. I have been so enthusiastic in my support that I have had more than one person ask me if I work for them. (I don't) 2. After a couple of months of trying everything, my wife asked me if we could return the dishwasher. I said, "Sure. No problem. It's Costco. They always make it right." Well, I did not know or recall than appliances have a 90 day return policy. Between summer travel, back to school, and work commitments, I just hadn't gotten around to dealing with it. Then I saw a Labor Day ad for $150 off of the Bosch 800 Series, which is essentially their top of the line. Well, it was 50% more expensive, but I was willing to give it a shot. I wasn't sure how to coordinate the return and replacement, because they usually pick up the old unit when they install the new one. So I called. As it turns out, I was FOUR DAYS over the 90 day return period. That's right - I requested a return on the 94th day. I genuinely believe the customer service representative tried his best. He kept coming back on the line and getting more information hoping to convince his supervisor to approve the return. They refused. I called back to speak to a supervisor, because I just couldn't believe Costco would do this. I wasn't able to actually speak to one, but the CSR said she was told that they are not authorized to make any exceptions to the 90 day return period. So, I have to say, my confidence in Costco is shaken. over 4 days.

Just something I was not expecting and would have though would be sturdier with the rest of the build quality on this.

It is quiet enough that you can easily have a conversation or even a whispered conversation right in front of it. I made my dishwasher even quieter by stuffing the gap between the top of my dishwasher and the underside of my countertop with a small piece of flexible foam insulation. Sentence (English): I got this dishwasher for a great price when sale was happening.
Comments (English): [ Very happy. Wonderful dishwasher. ] || ---------------- || I got this dishwasher for a great price when sale was happening. I had Best Buy deliver the dishwasher at a set scheduled time/day. The gentleman delivering were very kind, quick and efficient. They made sure to drop it off at the exact spot inside our house for my convenience. I had my husband remove the old dishwasher and install this one. FYI, he has never installed a dishwasher before but I am so proud of him, he said it actually wasn't complicated at all just tedious because we have a stupid but lovely kitchen lol. The dishwasher has many features & works very nicely, I love the bottle jets. My only complaint is that it states to use cascade dishwasher pods and they suck. Sometimes I will wash and the pod will not break up. I don't want to blame this dishwasher because it is very high quality. Due to this some cups and dishes are not fully sanitized or soap scum is left in the cups. The dishwasher instructions also recommended cascade liquid rinse aid, it kind of helps however, I am unsure if it dispenses the full amount that I put in (see pic). My mom has a dishwasher very similar to this one and she said her dishwasher does the same thing and doesn't always break up the pods properly. So she recommends to use cascade liquid detergent. It is kind of like a toothpaste blue gel scrub mixture that you squeeze out in the tray. She said ever since then she's never had any problems dishwashing. Unfortunately, I still have tons of pods lol, but will have to pick some up and maybe try a pod detergent mixture to get rid of the rest of these pods. As far as the liquid rinse aid, I feel like it's a scam, just like fabric softener lol.

Sentence (English): This is our 4th dishwasher in less than 8 years.
Comments (English): [ After a Month, So Far, So Good. ] || ---------------- || This is our 4th dishwasher in less than 8 years. The last one we purchased in June of 2022 and had to go through 4 service calls in the space of 12 months due to a design flaw. The outcome for 4th and final final service call was that it was no longer repairable. The problem for all the other units was the controls being located on the top edge of the door which allowed steam/heat to destroy the control panel. In households that run their dishwasher once a day or less perhaps this issue does not happen. However, in our situation it is run at least twice daily. We purchased this model specifically because the controls are on the front of the door, away from the steam & heat. Yeah, this time around we decided to give KitchenAid a try. I have rated it 4 stars because after 5 weeks there has not yet been any problems. Hopefully that will continue, but over the last 20 years, I have become more and more disillusioned with the quality of ALL major appliances marketed for the home market. So we're crossing our fingers and hoping for the best with KitchenAid.

Sentence (English): Samsung's dishwasher has become the worst appliance that I have ever owned.
Comments (English): [ Once good… no terrible ] || ---------------- || Samsung's dishwasher has become the worst appliance that I have ever owned. For the last 8 years, Samsung was my “go to”. I recommended it to all of my family and friends. However, things change! I have purchased 2 Samsung dishwashers over the past 2 years. The first one simply quit working (completely died) but due to past experiences, I thought it was a fluke and purchased an identical model. Now, my replacement is doing the exact same thing with no resolution. (I feel like I have been taken advantage of). In summary, not taking cost into consideration, I simply don't want the stress and responsibility of replacing a dishwasher every two years. I don't have the time to deal with the poor performance and a short lifespan. In addition, I don't like the fact that we have an appliance that needs to be tossed in the landfill every two years. What are we thinking? I just purchased a Bosch dishwasher for my second home. It seems to be more efficient and clean dishes better. I have had several friends that have recommended this brand, and I will be transitioning to Bosch in all of my homes.The worst part is; I convinced all of my friends that the Samsung dishwasher was the best choice for the price. However, price doesn't matter if something doesn't work. I now have to go back to them, and tell them, that it could possibly be the worst choice.SUCH A SHAME! I hope that Samsung's line of TVs continue to do as advertised. If not, Samsung will be a distant memory in my vocabulary.

Sentence (English): I had a Bosch that was made in Germany that ran quietly and worked great for 24 years.
Comments (English): [ Some Sadness ] || ---------------- || I had a Bosch that was made in Germany that ran quietly and worked great for 24 years. It was a beautiful bar front model - a classic rounded bar. The push button controls began to break down (after 24 years). I had no choice but to purchase a new one. I chose this model because I was looking for the simplest machine with the least bells and whistles and did not want the WIFI. I wanted a stainless tub and preferably the sleek bar front. I was disappointed to find that all the models with a stainless tub came with WIFI so I had no choice in that matter. The new bar front was square and in my opinion very unattractive so after reading all the various pros and cons I chose this model even though it was the newest one - attempting to avoid the issues Bosch was finding in the earlier models. This model was made in the USA. I would rather have had the German made model as their manufacturing quality seems to surpass ours in the US. With the ability to compare I found myself being disappointed in a few things, though overall satisfied. The quality parts of the machine have gone down. The door will bend if you move it from a side, rather than the solidity of my old machine's door. The drawers do not roll in and out as seemlessly as my old machine and they are of a thinner plastic. The basket for silverware is 1/2 the size so I am forced to use the top 3rd drawer. That's a nice option but you have to take your time and lay out each utensil which can prove time consuming and frustrating. The holder for the detergent feels cheap and I have doubts it'll last for many years. The controls work beautifully at the moment but as with any computerized item you fear, justifiably, that if it breaks down nothing will work and the entire control board would have to be replaced - a costly item I am sure. That is a difficult one to get over but no other choice is given. One thing I am very disappointed in is the drying. There is an option of "extra dry" and I use that with every wash cycle yet my coffee mugs are always wet. I tilt them as allowed by the model's design however I'm having to create an extreme tilt by my own design so water won't pool on the mugs. I never had that problem with my old machine. On the plus side it is very quiet - surpassing even my old quiet Bosch. It washes beautifully with no water spots (using the required rinse aid). Over time I will get over the downsides and be very happy with this choice. However I'm afraid I will always be leery of this computer board. My advise to Bosch is that they address my concerns and improve the manufacturing in the USA.

Sentence (English): I bought a Siemens dishwasher because I thought it was powerful.

I didn't know what to do with it after using it. It was very frustrating and disappointing. There was no instruction on how to use it, nor was he responsible for installing it. The carpenter just finished building the cabinet and put it in. He said he would never come back again and he would be charged for the next time. I really regret buying a Siemens dishwasher. I would have bought another brand if I had known this.

Sentence (English): I mostly like this dishwasher.
Comments (English): I mostly like this dishwasher. I have the bespoke fridge so I love the matching and glad to be rid of stainless. My main issue is that This dishwasher pops open at the end of the cycle but it just pops open a tiny amount to aid in drying. Because it's just cracked open, the steam escapes directly up underneath the edge of the countertop so the entire edge of my counter is soaked and dripping and the plywood beneath the marble is all wet, plus the control panel of the dishwasher is also soaked and dripping. We are going to have to pull the dishwasher forward so it cannot vent under the counter like that, but then it won't be recessed in to be even with the cabinets it will stick out ugly and awkward. I'm pretty bummed on that part. I find the racks inside to be poorly designed and top has weird angles to fit my dishes. I had a Bosch prior to this and loved the rack setup, I could fit way more dishes and in an organized way. So this is 4 stars for looks for me but 2 stars for very poor venting design and not the best rack setup.

Sentence (English): I am a fan of KitchenAid.
Comments (English): [ This one hit it out of the park! ] || ---------------- || I am a fan of KitchenAid. Let me be upfront about that. But my review is honest. I bought my house 2 years ago and the kitchen had all KitchenAid appliances. I had been to other homes and was amazed by the Bosch dishwashers I had seen because you could not hear them when they were running - just a little projected light on the floor. That's what I thought I wanted when it came time to replace my noisy, older KitchenAid in my vaulted ceiling, tiled floor house that carried sound all too well. I studied the specs of the KitchenAid, the Bosch, and the GE profile. I also learned from friends that the Boschs experienced service problems and premature breakdown issues. The KitchenAid, at 39 dBA was rated the quietest. It had all the features I needed and the 3rd rack was a nice bonus. I ordered it from Home Depot and it shipped and was installed 5 days later. It is beautiful and does a great job. We run it every day. It is so quiet that people open the door often because they didn't notice the blue light was on and just opened it to add an item. It is easy to forget since the old one could be heard 2 rooms away. The only thing you can hear is the water running down the drain under the kitchen sink occasionally as it flushes dirty water. That's it. I am totally satisfied with it. There are a few reviews that complain about water/steam venting out the front vent. We do not experience this at all. I love this dishwasher and I am completely happy with it and also my decision to buy it.

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher after my 10 year old whirlpool stopped working.
Comments (English): [ Leaves soapy residue on cups ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher after my 10 year old whirlpool stopped working. After researching different models on consumer reports, this Bosch 800 series seemed like the perfect one to get. Delivery and installation was great. the company called to schedule an approximate time for my delivery and called me 30 mins before showing up. The man who delivered and installed the unit was extremely curteous and even showed us how to use the dishwasher. After loading the dishwasher and starting the cycle, I was surprised at how quiet the unit is. There's a red light that shines on the floor to tell you that it is running since it is so quiet. Once the cycle completed, my husband and I unloaded the dishwasher and the dishes seemed very clean and we were both very happy. Later that day I went to get a glass of water and after filling it up, I noticed soapy bubbles. This was a few months ago. Ever since then, we have tried using several different types of dishwasher detergents including the recommened finish tablets. We have tried running cylces with and without finish rinse aid. We even called Bosch customer service and they sent out a technician who basically told us not to pre-rinse the dishes (we usually don't) and then told us to buy finish dishwasher cleaner. We did this and we still have soap bubbles on our cups after washes. So we are now left with either having to rinse all of our cups by hand after each load or run an extra rinse cycle after each load (which is fine, but then all the dishes are wet afterwards). This is not the end of the world but it is very frustrating, especially for the amount of money we spent on this machine.

I hope that Samsung's line of TVs continue to do as advertised. If not, Samsung will be a distant memory in my vocabulary.

There are three things we call the "three aunts" of our house: the dryer, the robot vacuum cleaner, and the dishwasher! We only had the dishwasher aunt in our house. We're a family of four, and even though it's a three-person dishwasher, except for large pots and pans, the dishwasher is just right and great. The dishwasher was delivered to my doorstep. I'm not very good with electronics, so I waited for my husband to come. After washing, the ventilation system takes care of everything from drying to storage, so you don't have to worry about moisture or odors. The 360-degree, two-stage, high-pressure rotating water jet cleans every nook and cranny, ensuring no blind spots. It's so clean and satisfying. There's even a separate water tank for collecting the water, which adds to the convenience. I tried it myself and found it really helpful, preventing water overflow. As long as it has a drain, you can place it anywhere. This no-touch, no-touch media dishwasher! With six cleaning modes, it offers standard, powerful, eco-steam sterilization, and quick presets. And washing dishes was actually so much fun, right? Since it's also storageable, there's no need for a dish drying rack. I just threw away the one I was using before~. This dishwasher is the best! Buy it, buy it again^^. This is a purchase review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Sentence (English): One of the biggest misconceptions about dishwashers is the sheer volume of water, electricity, and detergent, and the need for a pre-wash.
Comments (English): One of the biggest misconceptions about dishwashers is the sheer volume of water, electricity, and detergent, and the need for a pre-wash. Seriously, I used to think, "Why bother?" Seriously, I could just wash them all over. I'm lazy and just a little more diligent. Why bother? Then, at 50, I hit menopause, my knuckles started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't afford to invest this much in myself. Just then, I was selected for the test drive, and I was thrilled. I learned that there are even compact sizes for 3-4 people in small spaces. Recent models are said to be powerful and even eliminate the need for a pre-wash. I guess this is an improvement. Still, I personally think pre-washing dishes to remove grease and seasonings is a great way to avoid the hassle of a second manual cycle. Monthly electricity bills for six people are 2,000-3,000 won. For four people, one cycle costs less than 100 won, so let's put that burden aside for a moment. Opening soon~~~~~. Approximately 40cm in length, width, and height. It's a cube-shaped device with soft curves. Since our spoons are made of wood, we plan to use them without the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose is not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is easily tightened by inserting it into the drain hole. When manually filling the water, you must press the power button before filling to check the water tank alarm. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) uses a small amount of water and is suitable for basic washing, but it takes an hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick course (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) for 29 minutes. Unfortunately, there's no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. Also, you need to use a "washing detergent." Since this was my first time using this, I searched and found a detergent that worked well among those tested. You just place it on a simple square tray without a drain and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablets, they'll fall to the floor when you close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to work? (They just fall out). When washing larger dishes, the Secret Bar can be folded up to save space, and the wheels make it convenient, so you don't have to reach deep inside. It's not too noisy, and the suction from underneath seems quite strong. Hot water drains when the dishwasher drains. It's not so hot that you'll burn yourself, but you have to be careful. Being freed from the chore of washing dishes has improved my quality of life. Seeing clean, crisp dishes makes me smile, which is a nice touch. If you're feeling that way, I'd recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be great for 2-3 people in the future. It's a bit tight on space, and it's not meant for washing. A separate drying function would be even better. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.
Comments (Original): 사실상 식기세척기 오해중에 하나가 물,전기,세제 양이 많고 애벌설겆이를 하는데 굳이..참말로 그냥 씻어 엎으면되는걸 게을러서 조금만 부지런을 떨면될것을 굳이..왜..라고 생각했던 사람중 한사람이 접니다. 그런데 50에 갱년기가 겹치고 손가락 관절 마디마디가 쑤시기 시작했고 갑자기 인생사 뭐있나..나한테 이정도도 투자못하겠어~~지름신 함 불러내지 할때 체험단에 선정되어 신이 났습니다.작은공간에 3~4인기준 넘 아담한 사이즈도 있다는걸 알았네요. 요즘 나오는 모델들은 성능도 좋고 애벌설겆이를 안해도 깨끗한 세척이된다고 합니다. 개선이 된거겠죠.그래도 개인적인 생각으론 기름때나 벌건 양념은 애벌을 해주는게 2차 수작업으로 가지않는 번거로움 해결방법이지 않을까 싶어요.6인 기준으로 한달 전기요금이 2~3천원 나온대요. 4인기준 한번 돌리는데 백원 미만으로도 나올수 있다니 부담감은 잠시 접어두고~개봉박두~~~~~대충 가로 세로 높이가 40cm.부드러운 곡선의 큐브모양이예요.구성품중에 저흰 수저가 목재여서 수저통은 끼우지않고 사용하려합니다. 모든  식기가 세척에 적합하질않아 확인도 필수.입수호스는 연결하지않았고 배수호수는(길이145cm정도)배수구멍에 콕끼워 조임새로 쪼는 쉬운 방식입니다.수동급수시에는 '꼭' 전원버튼을 누른 후 급수를해야 물탱크 알림음 확인할수 있습니다.작동버튼중에 표준코스(세척65도-헹굼-헹굼70도-건조)가 물의 양이 적고 기본 세척에 적합하다는데 시간이 1시간이나 걸려서 시간이 짧은 쾌속 (세척55도-헹굼-헹굼60도)29분으로 사용해볼까 생각중입니다. 아쉬운건 건조 기능이없어 문을 열어 말려야합니다.또 '세척전용세제'를 써야된데요.첨인지라 검색을 해보니 세정제 실험한것중에 성능 좋은걸루 구매했어요.  주입구가 없는 그냥 사각 트레이 모양에  얹고 문을 닫아요.근데 액상이든 타블렛이든 문을 닫으면 바닥으로 떨어지겠는데 원래가 이런 방식인건가?(그냥 떨어지네요 ㅋㅋ)좀 큰그릇 세척시엔 시크릿바를 접을수 있어 공간활용도 되고 이동바퀴가 있어 깊숙이 손을 넣을 필요도 없이 편합니다.생활소음정도  크진않고 밑에서 쏘는 힘이 쎈가봐요. 배수때 뜨거운물이 빠져요.화상입을정도는 아니여도 조심해야겠습니다.설겆이라는 가사노동에서 해방되면서 맘적으로 삶의 질이 높아진 느낌이랄까...뽀득뽀득한 그릇을 보니 웃음이 나는게 기부니가 좋아졌어요. 이런 맘이면 식기세척기 추천해드리고 싶네요..추후-2~3인용으로 사용하면 좋을듯 싶어요. 공간이 살짝 부족하고 세척용도가 아닌  건조기능이 따로 추가가되면 더 좋겠어요 쿠팡체험단 이벤트로 상품을 무료로 제공 받아 작성한 구매 후기입니다.

Sentence (English): Seriously, I could just wash them all over.
Comments (English): One of the biggest misconceptions about dishwashers is the sheer volume of water, electricity, and detergent, and the need for a pre-wash. Seriously, I used to think, "Why bother?" Seriously, I could just wash them all over. I'm lazy and just a little more diligent. Why bother? Then, at 50, I hit menopause, my knuckles started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't afford to invest this much in myself. Just then, I was selected for the test drive, and I was thrilled. I learned that there are even compact sizes for 3-4 people in small spaces. Recent models are said to be powerful and even eliminate the need for a pre-wash. I guess this is an improvement. Still, I personally think pre-washing dishes to remove grease and seasonings is a great way to avoid the hassle of a second manual cycle. Monthly electricity bills for six people are 2,000-3,000 won. For four people, one cycle costs less than 100 won, so let's put that burden aside for a moment. Opening soon~~~~~. Approximately 40cm in length, width, and height. It's a cube-shaped device with soft curves. Since our spoons are made of wood, we plan to use them without the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose is not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is easily tightened by inserting it into the drain hole. When manually filling the water, you must press the power button before filling to check the water tank alarm. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) uses a small amount of water and is suitable for basic washing, but it takes an hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick course (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) for 29 minutes. Unfortunately, there's no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. Also, you need to use a "washing detergent." Since this was my first time using this, I searched and found a detergent that worked well among those tested. You just place it on a simple square tray without a drain and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablets, they'll fall to the floor when you close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to work? (They just fall out). When washing larger dishes, the Secret Bar can be folded up to save space, and the wheels make it convenient, so you don't have to reach deep inside. It's not too noisy, and the suction from underneath seems quite strong. Hot water drains when the dishwasher drains. It's not so hot that you'll burn yourself, but you have to be careful. Being freed from the chore of washing dishes has improved my quality of life. Seeing clean, crisp dishes makes me smile, which is a nice touch. If you're feeling that way, I'd recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be great for 2-3 people in the future. It's a bit tight on space, and it's not meant for washing. A separate drying function would be even better. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Sentence (English): Recent models are said to be powerful and even eliminate the need for a pre-wash.
Comments (English): One of the biggest misconceptions about dishwashers is the sheer volume of water, electricity, and detergent, and the need for a pre-wash. Seriously, I used to think, "Why bother?" Seriously, I could just wash them all over. I'm lazy and just a little more diligent. Why bother? Then, at 50, I hit menopause, my knuckles started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't afford to invest this much in myself. Just then, I was selected for the test drive, and I was thrilled. I learned that there are even compact sizes for 3-4 people in small spaces. Recent models are said to be powerful and even eliminate the need for a pre-wash. I guess this is an improvement. Still, I personally think pre-washing dishes to remove grease and seasonings is a great way to avoid the hassle of a second manual cycle. Monthly electricity bills for six people are 2,000-3,000 won. For four people, one cycle costs less than 100 won, so let's put that burden aside for a moment. Opening soon~~~~~. Approximately 40cm in length, width, and height. It's a cube-shaped device with soft curves. Since our spoons are made of wood, we plan to use them without the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose is not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is easily tightened by inserting it into the drain hole. When manually filling the water, you must press the power button before filling to check the water tank alarm. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) uses a small amount of water and is suitable for basic washing, but it takes an hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick course (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) for 29 minutes. Unfortunately, there's no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. Also, you need to use a "washing detergent." Since this was my first time using this, I searched and found a detergent that worked well among those tested. You just place it on a simple square tray without a drain and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablets, they'll fall to the floor when you close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to work? (They just fall out). When washing larger dishes, the Secret Bar can be folded up to save space, and the wheels make it convenient, so you don't have to reach deep inside. It's not too noisy, and the suction from underneath seems quite strong. Hot water drains when the dishwasher drains. It's not so hot that you'll burn yourself, but you have to be careful. Being freed from the chore of washing dishes has improved my quality of life. Seeing clean, crisp dishes makes me smile, which is a nice touch. If you're feeling that way, I'd recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be great for 2-3 people in the future. It's a bit tight on space, and it's not meant for washing. A separate drying function would be even better. Sentence (English): Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential.
Comments (English): One of the biggest misconceptions about dishwashers is the sheer volume of water, electricity, and detergent, and the need for a pre-wash. Seriously, I used to think, "Why bother?" Seriously, I could just wash them all over. I'm lazy and just a little more diligent. Why bother? Then, at 50, I hit menopause, my knuckles started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't afford to invest this much in myself. Just then, I was selected for the test drive, and I was thrilled. I learned that there are even compact sizes for 3-4 people in small spaces. Recent models are said to be powerful and even eliminate the need for a pre-wash. I guess this is an improvement. Still, I personally think pre-washing dishes to remove grease and seasonings is a great way to avoid the hassle of a second manual cycle. Monthly electricity bills for six people are 2,000-3,000 won. For four people, one cycle costs less than 100 won, so let's put that burden aside for a moment. Opening soon~~~~~. Approximately 40cm in length, width, and height. It's a cube-shaped device with soft curves. Since our spoons are made of wood, we plan to use them without the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose is not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is easily tightened by inserting it into the drain hole. When manually filling the water, you must press the power button before filling to check the water tank alarm. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) uses a small amount of water and is suitable for basic washing, but it takes an hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick course (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) for 29 minutes. Unfortunately, there's no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. Also, you need to use a "washing detergent." Since this was my first time using this, I searched and found a detergent that worked well among those tested. You just place it on a simple square tray without a drain and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablets, they'll fall to the floor when you close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to work? (They just fall out). When washing larger dishes, the Secret Bar can be folded up to save space, and the wheels make it convenient, so you don't have to reach deep inside. It's not too noisy, and the suction from underneath seems quite strong. Hot water drains when the dishwasher drains. It's not so hot that you'll burn yourself, but you have to be careful. Being freed from the chore of washing dishes has improved my quality of life. Seeing clean, crisp dishes makes me smile, which is a nice touch. If you're feeling that way, I'd recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be great for 2-3 people in the future. It's a bit tight on space, and it's not meant for washing. A separate drying function would be even better. Comments (English): One of the biggest misconceptions about dishwashers is the sheer volume of water, electricity, and detergent, and the need for a pre-wash. Then, at 50, I hit menopause, my knuckles started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't afford to invest this much in myself. Just then, I was selected for the test drive, and I was thrilled. I learned that there are even compact sizes for 3-4 people in small spaces. Recent models are said to be powerful and even eliminate the need for a pre-wash. I guess this is an improvement. Still, I personally think pre-washing dishes to remove grease and seasonings is a great way to avoid the hassle of a second manual cycle. Monthly electricity bills for six people are 2,000-3,000 won. For four people, one cycle costs less than 100 won, so let's put that burden aside for a moment. Opening soon~~~~~. Approximately 40cm in length, width, and height. It's a cube-shaped device with soft curves. Since our spoons are made of wood, we plan to use them without the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose is not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is easily tightened by inserting it into the drain hole. When manually filling the water, you must press the power button before filling to check the water tank alarm. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) uses a small amount of water and is suitable for basic washing, but it takes an hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick course (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) for 29 minutes. Unfortunately, there's no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. Also, you need to use a "washing detergent." Since this was my first time using this, I searched and found a detergent that worked well among those tested. You just place it on a simple square tray without a drain and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablets, they'll fall to the floor when you close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to work? (They just fall out). When washing larger dishes, the Secret Bar can be folded up to save space, and the wheels make it convenient, so you don't have to reach deep inside. It's not too noisy, and the suction from underneath seems quite strong. Hot water drains when the dishwasher drains. It's not so hot that you'll burn yourself, but you have to be careful. Being freed from the chore of washing dishes has improved my quality of life. Seeing clean, crisp dishes makes me smile, which is a nice touch. If you're feeling that way, I'd recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be great for 2-3 people in the future. It's a bit tight on space, and it's not meant for washing. A separate drying function would be even better. Sentence (English): Seeing clean, crisp dishes makes me smile, which is a nice touch.
Comments (English): One of the biggest misconceptions about dishwashers is the sheer volume of water, electricity, and detergent, and the need for a pre-wash. Seriously, I used to think, "Why bother?" Seriously, I could just wash them all over. I'm lazy and just a little more diligent. Why bother? Then, at 50, I hit menopause, my knuckles started to ache, and I suddenly thought, "What's the point of life? I can't afford to invest this much in myself. Just then, I was selected for the test drive, and I was thrilled. I learned that there are even compact sizes for 3-4 people in small spaces. Recent models are said to be powerful and even eliminate the need for a pre-wash. I guess this is an improvement. Still, I personally think pre-washing dishes to remove grease and seasonings is a great way to avoid the hassle of a second manual cycle. Monthly electricity bills for six people are 2,000-3,000 won. For four people, one cycle costs less than 100 won, so let's put that burden aside for a moment. Opening soon~~~~~. Approximately 40cm in length, width, and height. It's a cube-shaped device with soft curves. Since our spoons are made of wood, we plan to use them without the spoon holder. Not all dishes are suitable for washing, so checking is essential. The inlet hose is not connected, and the drain hose (about 145cm long) is easily tightened by inserting it into the drain hole. When manually filling the water, you must press the power button before filling to check the water tank alarm. Among the operation buttons, the standard course (wash 65 degrees - rinse - rinse 70 degrees - dry) uses a small amount of water and is suitable for basic washing, but it takes an hour, so I'm thinking of using the quick course (wash 55 degrees - rinse - rinse 60 degrees) for 29 minutes. Unfortunately, there's no drying function, so you have to open the door to dry it. Also, you need to use a "washing detergent." Since this was my first time using this, I searched and found a detergent that worked well among those tested. You just place it on a simple square tray without a drain and close the door. But whether it's liquid or tablets, they'll fall to the floor when you close the door. Is this the way it's supposed to work? (They just fall out). When washing larger dishes, the Secret Bar can be folded up to save space, and the wheels make it convenient, so you don't have to reach deep inside. It's not too noisy, and the suction from underneath seems quite strong. Hot water drains when the dishwasher drains. It's not so hot that you'll burn yourself, but you have to be careful. Being freed from the chore of washing dishes has improved my quality of life. Seeing clean, crisp dishes makes me smile, which is a nice touch. If you're feeling that way, I'd recommend a dishwasher. I think it would be great for 2-3 people in the future. It's a bit tight on space, and it's not meant for washing. A separate drying function would be even better. This is a review written after receiving the product for free as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

It feels like it was designed for many scenarios, but I have a harder time using the space than with my previous dishwasher that had simply two lanes with good spacing. Final thoughts: I would still buy this model and I recommend it, but I hope they review the arrangement of the bottom drawer for future model options.

Sentence (English): Pros: Cleans well, and very quiet.

More important is that coupler for sink does NOT FIT FLUSH in the space in back of machine. This means machine cannot be pushed flush against wall to align with other cabinets, but also puts wall at risk for damage and coupler at risk for being broken. We've had to jerry-rig some bumpers on wall. Really stupid design flaw, and one that we couldn't see until machine delivered because store does not have portable dishwashers on display (can only buy online). Shame on you, GE.

Sentence (English): We've had this for a month now, but we had the exact same one before we moved.
Comments (English): We've had this for a month now, but we had the exact same one before we moved. I loved it so much that I decided to buy the same one so that I wouldn't have to shop around again. It's quiet and there is a small third rack for utensils and other smaller things like medicine cups, straws, etc. There is a basket on the bottom for all of that as well, but the top rack is big enough for all my utensils so I take the basket out so that there is more room on the bottom for bigger dishes. The adjustable middle rack is great for when I can't put water bottles on the bottom rack. I just lower the middle rack so that they can fit there. I still have to tilt bigger water bottles, but I can't put the thin plastic ones on the bottom or the heat ruins their shape. It dries the dishes very well if you add jet dry to it, but I don't like using jet dry so my plastic cups don't dry completely so I just leave them out for a little bit to dry. Glass dries great though and there are no water stains left on them.

Sentence (English): We ordered this in fall of '22.
Comments (English): [ decent dish washer with a terrible flaw ] || ---------------- || We ordered this in fall of '22. It installed pretty easily and has performed well (I installed it myself). There was a minor leaking issue right away that I quickly determined was a faulty door seal that caused condensation to collect and drip down and out of the front corner of the washer. I was able to schedule a repair and it was covered by the warranty, and haven't had any other issues since with one exception: the feet. Whoever decided the foot style for this dishwasher was okay needs to be fired. instead of the standard metal threads with lock nut that most dishwashers have, this dish washer has all plastic leveling feet that fit loosely and have no locking mechanism, meaning that over time the legs slowly rotate and the machine lowers itself. absolutely infuriating. There was a minor leaking issue right away that I quickly determined was a faulty door seal that caused condensation to collect and drip down and out of the front corner of the washer. I was able to schedule a repair and it was covered by the warranty, and haven't had any other issues since with one exception: the feet. Whoever decided the foot style for this dishwasher was okay needs to be fired. instead of the standard metal threads with lock nut that most dishwashers have, this dish washer has all plastic leveling feet that fit loosely and have no locking mechanism, meaning that over time the legs slowly rotate and the machine lowers itself. absolutely infuriating. I'm trying to come up with a solution that doesn't include lowering the feet all the way and wedging wood underneath them. an absolute disaster of a design on an otherwise fine dishwasher. also the plastic on the buttons started to bubble and wear away already and we use this thing very lightly and treat it with care. overall we're satisfied. it's annoying that we payed $900 for it and it's now on sale for $550, but it has been fine so far. I'd be giving it 4 stars if the feet weren't so horrendous. not sure why nobody else has mentioned this, perhaps they just haven't noticed that it's gone out of level.

Sentence (English): The three new home appliances that will change your quality of life are a dishwasher, dryer, and robot vacuum cleaner.
Comments (English): [ Single-person household review - convenient but a little noisy ] || ---------------- || The three new home appliances that will change your quality of life are a dishwasher, dryer, and robot vacuum cleaner. Since I live alone, I don't think I'll have much to wash, but when I cook kimbap or other dishes, there are times when I end up washing more dishes than I thought. I chose this product expecting the convenience of being able to do other things while washing the dishes. I wondered if the dishwasher would do the same, just as the washing machine improved my quality of life when I used to wash my clothes by hand. The advantages are 1. The glass door makes it easy to see how it's working from inside. It stops in the middle and can adjust the position of the dishes. 2. It has five practical washing modes. It washes well. When I washed it by hand, the milk smell didn't come out well, but after washing and sterilizing, the tumbler container became clean - however, larval washing is essential for severe cases. You have to put the dishes evenly (this is a bit annoying, and if you put in one noodle bowl, the rest of the dishes don't fit well, so there's not enough space) 3. It's convenient because you can turn on the 72-hour circulation drying system and leave it as is after going out. 4. No construction required, manual water supply It's an advantage because you don't have to do separate construction, but it's also a disadvantage because you have to manually fill 5L of water. This may vary from person to person. It's an advantage based on my house. The disadvantages are 1. Because I try to spread the dishes evenly, the space isn't wide. If you put in one noodle bowl, only a spoon, small bowl, and cup can fit. It may be a little narrow for 3 people. (Of course, if you only put in rice and soup bowls, 3 people will barely be able to fit? It's impossible if you add side dish bowls.) However, the outside is large compared to the inside space, so it feels like it takes up a lot of space for 1 person? I recommend it even if you live alone and have a wide sink. 2. A little noisy. Personally, I think it's louder than a drum washing machine when it's washing. It's hard to run it at night. It seems suitable for running right before work or during the day. 3. It is not completely dry. When it is finished, there is a wind noise, but there is still moisture. It is definitely cleaner (protein shake milk residue smell removed!), and it is convenient because you can do other things during that time. However, you still have to hand wash things like frying pans, pots, and cutting boards, and the time it takes to run the machine is about 5-6 times longer than just washing dishes, so you should decide whether to buy it or not depending on your personal lifestyle. I don't know about the electricity bill because I haven't used it for long. I know that dishwashers don't use much electricity. I don't know about this product. I run it almost every day, but I will add a review if the electricity bill goes up. ------------------------ Review after 6 weeks of use 1. It doesn't use much electricity. 2. It removes the smell from the shake container and coffee tumbler well after drinking protein shakes. 3. Pots and frying pans don't go in, so you have to wash them by hand. Regular dishes also have to be washed every time to remove red pepper powder, etc. 4. It is very loud. Especially at night. Conclusion! -> The dishes and cups are washed and sterilized, so they are definitely clean. Deodorization is good. Highly recommended for washing cups such as tumblers -> The pretreatment process can be annoying. This may vary from person to person. It's an advantage based on my house. The disadvantages are 1. Because I try to spread the dishes evenly, the space isn't wide. If you put in one noodle bowl, only a spoon, small bowl, and cup can fit. It may be a little narrow for 3 people. (Of course, if you only put in rice and soup bowls, 3 people will barely be able to fit? It's impossible if you add side dish bowls.) However, the outside is large compared to the inside space, so it feels like it takes up a lot of space for 1 person? I recommend it even if you live alone and have a wide sink. 2. A little noisy.
